case_name: Sarabjeet Singh and Others v State of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

22 November 1982
Cr.A. No. 608 of 1982 (Arising out of SPL (Cri.) No. 2077 of 1982) (Cr.A. No. 542 of 1976, D/- 26 March 1982, (All) (LB.))
The Order of the Court is as follows:
Special leave granted.
We heard Mr. Ram Jethmalani, learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the State of U.P.

facts: The appellant Sarabjeet Singh and 17 other persons were put up on trial before the learned II Additional Sessions Judge, Gonda, in Sessions Trial No. A-65/74 for having committed offences under Sections 147, 427 read with 149, 323 read with 149 and 302 read with 149 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

The genesis of the quarrel lies in a transaction of sale of land belonging to one Smt. Koela purchased by P.W. 1 Ghirau from accused 1 Sarabjeet Singh for a consideration of Rs. 1600/- three years prior to July 15, 1972, being the date of occurrence.

On July 15, 1972, P.W. 1 Ghirau, his other son P.W. 2 Pateshwari Prasad, his mother Smt. Koela and his wife Smt. Patiraji were present on their ancestral land in front of his house and the infant Radhey Shyam was playing, near about.
At that time, led by accused 1, 17 other named accused and some others unknown and unidentified about 5-6 in number trespassed into the land.
issues: Whether the learned Sessions Judge was right in convicting accused 1 for an offence under S. 302, Indian Penal Code, 1860
The nature of the offence and sentence in respect of accused 1 Sarabjeet Singh
petitioner_arguments: Accused 1 pleaded that he has been falsely involved in the case on account of a conspiracy between Lalta Prasad and Ghirau with a view to taking away the land which was in his possession for years.
He stated that Plot No. 1145 has been in his possession since the time of his father and this plot came to be recorded in the name of his mother during consolidation operations.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution case that Radhey Shyam suffered some internal injuries and vomited blood and soon fell into coma.
The learned Sessions Judge held accused 1 Sarabjeet Singh guilty of having committed the murder of Radhey Shyam and convicted and sentenced him to suffer imprisonment for life.
court_reasoning: We would accept that without a demur. Turning to the medical evidence, P.W. 7 Dr. Nirankar Singh, Surgeon Incharge of the Civil Hospital, Gonda, deposed that he carried out the autopsy on the dead body of Radhey Shyam.
According to the opinion of the Surgeon deceased died in coma and death was caused due to brain injury.
holding: We grant leave limited to the question as set out in the notice. The limited inquiry, therefore, in this case is whether the learned Sessions Judge was right in convicting accused 1 for an offence under S. 302, Indian Penal Code, 1860 and the High Court in confirming the same in the circumstances of this case.
